title: Researchers Impersonate RSA HSM to Forge Signatures Without Extracting Private Key
content_md: A newly disclosed practical attack can impersonate a hardware security module (HSM) and forge arbitrary 1024-bit RSA signatures without extracting or factoring the device’s private key. The research, titled Forging 1024-bit RSA Signatures in Nearly SNFS Time , implements a two-decade-old cryptanalytic technique against raw RSA signing and decryption oracles. The method allows an attacker with temporary access to an HSM’s unpadded RSA signing function to perform a large precomputation and query-collection operation, then permanently generate valid signatures offline for that RSA key. Researchers Impersonate RSA HSM The attack does not recover the RSA private exponent or factor the public modulus. Instead, it exploits access to raw RSA root operations, effectively turning limited oracle access into the long-term capability to sign arbitrary target values. The attack model resembles a “lunchtime” or non-adaptive chosen-ciphertext scenario. An attacker first obtains temporary access to an RSA signing or decryption oracle for a known public key. Once access is lost, the attacker can still forge signatures or decrypt chosen ciphertexts offline. Researchers instantiated the oracle using HSMs through PKCS#11 raw RSA operations, specifically the CKM_RSA_X_509 mechanism.
